subject: Network fencing & dataflow mapping — security next steps for NexaHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Network fencing & dataflow mapping — security next steps for NexaHealth

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items: 

Call highlights:
- NexaHealth is evaluating a private/VPC deployment for PHI workloads and wants isolation from public endpoints.
- Priority requirements: HIPAA compliance, audit logging retention (minimum 12 months), customer-managed KMS, and network-level egress controls.
- SOC 2 status: you mentioned SOC 2 Type II in progress with a target completion in Q3.

Action items (next steps):
1) Please share any available SOC 2 evidence or an attestation timeline (SOC 2 in progress is ok). If you can provide the SOC 2 roadmap & expected completion date, we can map gating items.
2) Attach a high-level network/dataflow diagram that shows: ingress paths, where PHI is stored/processed, existing VPN or DirectConnect links, and any on-prem components that must be isolated.
3) Nexa to complete the short vendor security questionnaire we attached. This will help our security and engineering teams size the private deployment and flag any air-gap constraints.
4) We'll follow up with a short design options doc: (a) VPC peering + private endpoints, (b) Dedicated on-prem appliance (colocated), (c) Air-gapped deployment. We'll include cost/operational tradeoffs.

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire-v1.pdf (please fill & return), example redwood-private-deploy-checklist.pdf

Would you be able to share the dataflow diagram and SOC 2 timeline by EOD Tuesday (May 21)? If not, propose an alternate date.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben and Sean for the technical/ops details once we have the diagram.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — "Predictable, economical LLM inference for production""

From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@nexahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, NexaHealth Security Team <security@nexahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 10:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Network fencing & dataflow mapping — security next steps for NexaHealth

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the questionnaire. We had a productive internal sync. Quick answers and what we attached: 

What we shared:
- Attached: nexaflow_v1.pdf (high-level dataflow diagram) — includes PHI processing boundary and our EHR connector.
- SOC 2: currently underway; Type II expected by 2028-09-15. We can provide interim controls evidence (control matrix export) by Wednesday.

Notes / clarifications:
- PHI stores live in our on-prem SAN behind our firewall; processing happens in a Kubernetes cluster in our VPC. We use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys.
- We do have an existing ExpressRoute/DirectConnect to our cloud provider in some regions; details are in the diagram.
- Air-gapped: we have a separate QA lab that is physically isolated; production air-gap would require approval and Ops time (estimate 6–8 weeks setup).

Next steps from our side:
- Fill your vendor questionnaire and return by EOD Wednesday (May 23).
- Share any specific compliance artifacts (audit log schema, retention policy) you need and we'll try to extract them.

Attachment: nexaflow_v1.pdf (diagram).

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if you want us to walk through the diagram.

—
Elena Martin
VP, Product & Security
Elena.Martin@nexahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0133

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor questionnaire & quick design clarifications

Elena — appreciate the diagram and SOC 2 timeline. Couple of follow-ups from engineering/security to speed the sizing exercise: 

1) Questionnaire: thanks — if you could return the vendor-security-questionnaire-v1.pdf with answers inline, that will let us do a gap-map quickly.

2) Data residency / egress: Can you confirm whether backups are stored in the same VPC region as processing, and whether any backups are exported to third-party storage? This impacts our retention and key management recommendations.

3) Network options: to set expectations on tradeoffs we plan to include in our design doc: 
   - Option A: Private VPC endpoints + strict SGs (fastest to deploy, minimal Ops)
   - Option B: Dedicated capacity in a customer VPC with DirectConnect/MPLS (medium Ops, stronger isolation)
   - Option C: On-prem appliance or air-gapped deployment (high Ops, longest lead time).

4) Air-gap specifics: If production needs to be air-gapped, do you require physical-only transfer (sneakernet) for model updates, or can updates be delivered via a one-way data diode? Any constraints here change rollout cadence.

5) Audit logs & retention: we support configurable retention; can you indicate required retention in months? You mentioned 12 months earlier — please confirm.

If you prefer, we can send a short checklist for each option so your infrastructure team can mark feasibility quickly.

Thanks — cc'ing Sean (solutions engineer) who will prepare the options doc once we get these clarifications.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@nexahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, NexaHealth Security Team <security@nexahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 16:33:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire & quick design clarifications

Ben / team — answering inline: 

1) We'll return the questionnaire by COB Thursday (May 24).
2) Backups: backups are stored in the same region as processing; we also replicate to an S3 bucket in a secondary region for DR. No third-party exports by default.
3) Air-gap: production air-gap would require physical-only media for model artifacts per our compliance team; a one-way diode is acceptable for non-PHI models but not for PHI processing without additional controls.
4) Retention: Confirmed 12 months for audit logs; we can provide a sample schema for the logging events.

Separately — can Redwood share the on-prem deployment checklist you referenced? We'd like to review hardware/network pre-reqs so procurement can start parallel tasks.

Thanks — we'll attach the completed questionnaire and a slightly updated nexaflow_v1b.pdf later this week.

—
Elena Martin
VP, Product & Security
NexaHealth
